topSignals.title: FCEL surges 27.5%, Bloom drops 12% in sharpest fuel cell rotation of 2026
topSignals.text: — On June 26, Jefferies upgraded FuelCell Energy from Hold to Buy with a $24 PT (from $16), arguing FCEL trades at ~8x 2030 EV/EBITDA vs. Bloom at ~19x — a "compelling asymmetric entry" following the Fit Energy 380 MW deal and planned $200–275M Torrington expansion to 350–500 MW/year. UBS simultaneously tripled its FCEL PT to $22 (Neutral, from $7.25). Capital rotated hard: FCEL +27.5% (best single-day gain in over a year); Bloom sank 12%+ to ~$268 close (range $264.50–$299.60), its largest single-day decline of the 2026 rally. Jefferies upgrade / MarketBeat | FCEL / Yahoo Finance | BE plunge / TipRanks

topSignals.title: Microsoft + Chevron "Project Kilby": 2.67 GW dedicated natural gas plant for West Texas AI campus
topSignals.text: — 20-year PPA signed June 22; GE Vernova + Solar Turbines (Caterpillar) to power Microsoft's Reeves County, TX data center; final investment decision by end-2026; first power 2028; entirely behind-the-meter (no grid tie, no ITC 48E). First GW-class dedicated CCGT project for an AI data center — strongest signal yet that gas turbines are a direct competitive threat to SOFCs at ≥2 GW scale where 2-year lead times are acceptable. TechCrunch | CNBC | Chevron PR

topSignals.title: DOE commits $17.5B to 10 large nuclear reactors, citing AI data center demand
topSignals.text: — Announced June 23; five low-interest loans for long-lead-time component procurement (pressure vessels, steam generators) for 10 Westinghouse 1.1 GW AP1000 reactors. Goal: all 10 under construction by 2030; hyperscalers named as principal customers. Reinforces nuclear as the dominant long-term alternative to SOFCs (>10 year horizon), now with direct federal financing. PBS News | GovCIO | Latitude Media

items.text: EFCF 2026 opens in 3 days (Monday June 30) — 17th European SOFC & SOE Forum, Lucerne. First technical results expected from European players (Ceres licensees, Elcogen, SolydEra, Convion). See prior digests for background. EFCF

FuelCell Energy 12.5 MW "Energy Block" (first appearance in digest) — FCEL's March 2026 product packages ten 1.25 MW molten carbonate modules into a single data-center unit; reduces site engineering and permitting overhead; Torrington factory scaling from ~100 MW to 350–500 MW/year with $200–275M capex over 24 months. Note: FCEL uses MCFC (molten carbonate), not SOFC — different stack chemistry (~60% electrical efficiency, ~650°C vs. SOFC's 800°C), but competes in the same data center power procurement market. GlobeNewswire | StockTitan

Project Kilby (CCGT) context — See Top Signal #2. At ≥2 GW scale and 2-year acceptable lead time, CCGT competes directly with SOFC. SOFCs retain the advantage for <500 MW projects or where 90-day grid-bypass speed is the critical constraint.
Quiet day on net-new SOFC deployment announcements. Prior deals (Oracle/Jupiter 2.45 GW, Crusoe/Cheyenne 900 MW Phase 1, Equinix >100 MW, FCEL/Fit Energy 380 MW, Bloom/Brookfield $5B) unchanged.

Section 179D: 3 days to construction-begin deadline (Tuesday June 30) — Last-chance weekend for co-located fuel cell + data center projects to break ground. Projects must begin significant physical work or spend >=5% of total project cost by June 30. (Full context covered in June 26 digest.) energystackhub.com
DOE nuclear loan context — Component procurement loans only (not construction financing); no near-term SOFC market impact, but strong federal intent signal for nuclear as the >2030 alternative.

Microsoft + Chevron Project Kilby (2.67 GW CCGT, Texas, first power 2028) — See Top Signal #2. No grid tie; no ITC 48E for gas plant. At ~$1,600–2,200/kW CCGT capex and $4–6/MMBtu gas: LCOE ~$45–85/MWh — far below SOFC even after ITC 48E (~$90–140/MWh with CHP). SOFC wins on speed (90 days vs. 24+ months), NOx reduction, and modularity; CCGT wins on raw economics at multi-GW committed scale with adequate lead time. TechCrunch | Bloomberg
DOE $17.5B nuclear program — 10+ year delivery horizon. Not a near-term SOFC competitor but a material long-run risk for the 2030+ market.

Bloom Energy (BE) — June 26 close ~$268.25 (range $264.50–$299.60), down 12%+ from June 25's ~$326 close; largest single-day decline of the 2026 AI data center rally. Now trading below both analyst price targets (Barclays $276 EW; UBS $322 Buy). 52-week range: $21.50–$351.28. Market citing Project Kilby (CCGT competition) and DOE nuclear loans as catalysts for the de-rating. TipRanks | Yahoo Finance

FuelCell Energy (FCEL) — +27.5% on June 26; best single-day gain in >1 year. Jefferies: Buy, $24 PT (valuation: 8x vs. Bloom's 19x 2030 EV/EBITDA). UBS: Neutral, $22 PT (tripled from $7.25). Torrington expansion ($200–275M, 350–500 MW/year capacity) underpins the upgrade thesis. FCEL pipeline +275% since Feb 2025, majority from data center customers. MarketBeat | GuruFocus | Yahoo Finance / UBS

Forschungszentrum Jülich 93,000-hour SOFC milestone (RSC JMC-A, 2025) — Atomic-scale study of air electrode degradation in short stack F1002-97 operated for 93,000 hours (~10.6 years) at 700°C under constant current (0.5 A/cm²). Confirms 0.5%/1000h degradation rate is achievable in real-world extended operation; identifies Sr and La migration in LSCF cathode as the dominant long-term failure mechanism; plasma-spray protective coatings and in-situ sintering identified as key mitigations. RSC JMC-A
Watch: EFCF opens Monday June 30 — Expect new stack durability, efficiency, and manufacturing cost data from European developers.

lcoe.text: Rystad Energy: SOFC system capex -20-25% by 2030 — Driven by Bloom 2 GW Fremont ramp and FCEL Torrington expansion; Rystad projects 10.4 GW cumulative fuel cell demand from data centers 2026–2030 and market revenues growing to ~$30B by 2030. At 20-25% cost reduction from current $6,000–7,200/kW: implied 2030 capex ~$4,500–5,400/kW unsubsidized; ~$3,150–3,780/kW after ITC 48E. Recommend adding 2030 low-capex sensitivity case to LCOE model. Rystad Energy | Gas to Power Journal

Project Kilby CCGT benchmark: 2.67 GW dedicated behind-the-meter gas plant, 20-year PPA, first power 2028. Implied capex ~$1,600–2,200/kW → LCOE ~$45–85/MWh at $4–6/MMBtu gas. SOFC LCOE gap vs. CCGT: ~$45–95/MWh even with ITC 48E + CHP. Economic case for SOFC rests on speed + NOx reduction + modularity, not cost parity at multi-GW scale.

Jülich 93,000h durability: at 0.5%/1000h degradation, stack reaches ~46% performance retention at 10.6 years — validates 10-year stack replacement interval (vs. the conservative 5-year schedule sometimes modeled). Extending from 5 to 10 year stack life reduces O&M costs by ~15–20% in a 20-year project NPV.
